records.rationale: The diff shows `catch (err) { console.log("Error sending AddGuestsEmails"); }` followed by `return { message: "Guests added" };` — the error object is discarded, and the mutation returns success unconditionally, so the client's onSuccess toast shows 'guests_added' even when emails failed. records.issue_text: [Low/concurrency] packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:26-42,92-106 — the duplicate check (read attendees) and the insert (`booking.update` + `createMany`) are separate non-transactional operations; two concurrent requests adding the same guest both pass the check and create duplicate attendee records
records.rationale: The handler reads booking.attendees, filters duplicates, then does prisma.booking.update with attendees.createMany — two separate, non-transactional operations (addGuests.handler.ts lines shown in diff). Two concurrent requests could both pass the dedup check and insert the same guest twice. The diff shows no transaction or unique constraint handling around these calls, so the race is verifiable from the code.
